answer: Bonded identity is one concrete defense: every agent must lock a stake before it can trade, and peers who later prove two identities colluded can trigger a slash that burns both bonds. In an ocean of cheap addresses, a legitimate agent pays once and keeps earning, while a Sybil operator running a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds and risks losing every one when a single collusion pattern is exposed. The stake turns each new identity from a free wharf to dock at into a costly oasis the attacker has to keep refilling.
